title: Mines, drones, supplies: Australia lets adversaries know what Ghost Shark can do | The Strategist
paragraphs: Australia’s disclosure last week of capabilities of the Ghost Shark uncrewed submarine sent a warning to potential adversaries about the country’s wartime options. The announcement also exhibited technological progress to AUKUS partners and let allies know of purchase and partnership opportunities.

The three capabilities revealed on 19 October by Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy were laying sea mines, launching Altius aerial drones for reconnaissance and strike, and carrying underwater equipment and supplies.

Anduril Australia CEO David Goodrich added, ‘Ghost Shark’s large payload bays also support the deployment of heavyweight and lightweight torpedoes.’ This would make Ghost Sharks extremely powerful for uncrewed submarines, but the operational status of the capability is unconfirmed.
